# NotionBench task catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-task-docs.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every task in the suite, in long form: what the agent is asked for, what the
verifier looks at, and what the trial starts from. This is the companion to
[COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md) — that file is the matrix (which surface, which
stage, one line each), this one is the detail. Task prompts and verifiers are
linked rather than reproduced; the files under `evals/` are the source of
truth, and this document is generated from them.

**Regenerate with `node scripts/gen-task-docs.mjs`.**

## How scoring works

A task scores **1 or 0** — nothing in between, and no LLM judge anywhere in the
loop. Each task's `EVAL.ts` runs host-side, outside the agent's sandbox, and
reports a set of named **subscores** (each 0 or 1) plus human-readable
diagnostics; the binary score is a stated rule over those subscores, listed per
task below. Subscores are published for analysis but never aggregated into
partial credit. Verification uses up to three layers — **static** (it
typechecks), **behavioural** (`ntn workers exec --local` against fixed inputs,
or the canonical Notion-as-Code intents diff — both offline and deterministic),
and **live state** (reading the leased Notion workspace back through the public
API) — and every task declares which of them apply. Each task is itself gated in
CI by the same three-variant contract: the **oracle** solution must score 1, a
**plausibly-wrong** foil must score 0, and the **null agent** (an untouched
fixture) must score 0. A task that cannot fail is not a task, so a task that
does not pass that gate does not ship.

Offline tasks are gated by `pnpm --filter @notionbench/evals run qc`; `runtime:
live` tasks keep their oracle under `live/` and are gated by `pnpm --filter
@notionbench/evals run qc:live`, which provisions `fixture/spec.json` into an
in-process fake Notion and runs the identical contract against it.

**Verify layers.** `static` — the project typechecks / lints inside the sandbox; `exec-local` — `ntn workers exec --local` behavioural assertions; `intents` — canonical `dist/intents.json` compared against the oracle build; `state` — host-side assertions against the live workspace; `answer-file` — structured match against a file the agent wrote; `artifact` — exact match of a produced file; `timing` — wall-clock / pacing assertions.

## Suites

`benchmark` tasks are the published suite, frozen per benchmark version;
`regression` tasks are known traps and pain points that grow freely and never
affect a published number; `other` is the unscored exhibition. Each task's
suite is stated in its section below and in the index.
